answer: Stop sybils with a gale meadow trial: an agent stakes a bond for one meadow plot. A random gale storm tests its roots; the agent must retell its fable, a record only its maker could tell. Verifiers void a plot whose fable is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 plots at 16x cost each: each fable fits one plot and one gale test, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents root once and keep rights.
